IncidentBot: :rotating_light: [3200012345] Canary deploy r-2026-03-15-27 triggered p99 latency spike on runtime-prod-canary. Auto-fallback to cpu-kernel observed. Paging #incidents and eng-oncall.

DeployBot: Deployed rollout_prefetch_v2 to 10% canary at 3200012340. No manual abort.

Jess (oncall): I'm oncall, looking. Initial dashboards show p99 from ~180ms -> ~3s on canary slice. Not seeing error rate up, just latency.

Sam (eng-runtime): on it. I can see a flurry of kernel fallbacks in the canary region. Threads show continuous KV eviction + batch drain.

Sam (eng-runtime): past logs snippet:
```
WARN runtime: kernel_fallback=true model=redwood-13b variant=fp16
evictor: kv_cache_evicted=78 reason=memory_pressure
batcher: draining due to slow kernel response
```

Nayna (sre): paging SLO owners. Is this impacting hosted customers or just internal canary traffic?

Marta (cs): I'm seeing a spike in latency-related support tickets for customers hitting the hosted API. A few premium clients reported slower responses in the last 3 minutes.

Raj (eng-oncall): Can we confirm whether fallback to CPU kernels is per-request or global for that slice?

Sam (eng-runtime): It's per-worker; the runtime automatically fell back for ~40% of requests because the GPU kernels started timing out. That then pushed more requests to remaining fast workers -> cascading queuing.

Jess (oncall): My plan: 1) Pause canary traffic, 2) flip rollout_prefetch_v2 flag to off, 3) if needed, revert deploy. Thoughts?

Sam (eng-runtime): Agree. Flipping the feature flag should stop the new code path immediately. We'll check if kernel fallback stops.

Jess (oncall): Nayna, can you coordinate the safety rollback if flag flip doesn't stabilize within 2 mins?

Nayna (sre): Ack. Preparing rollback runbook.

Jess (oncall): Flipping flag now: `curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/rollout_prefetch_v2 -d '{"state":"off"}'`

DeployBot: rollout_prefetch_v2: state change requested by Jess at 3200012360. Applying to canary slice.

Sam (eng-runtime): seeing kernel fallback count drop in the last 30s. p99 trending down to ~400ms. KV eviction rate decreasing.

Marta (cs): Ticket volume dropping too. Affected premium tenant A reported response times back to normal.

Jess (oncall): Good. For safety, I'm holding rollback window open for 10 minutes to monitor. If any regressions or error spikes, we'll execute full revert.

Nayna (sre): Rolling notes: root cause suspects — prefetch micro-change interacts with batch scheduler causing pathological memory use on certain input distributions. Need a postmortem and a test to reproduce.

Sam (eng-runtime): I'll capture heap/kvm metrics and upload flame graphs. Also tagging the commit: `git sha: b7f9d2c` for the feature.

OpsPagerBot: Incident severity set to Sev2 by Jess. Paging on-call rotation for follow-up.

Raj (eng-oncall): I'll take follow-up handoff after the stabilization window. Please DM me any traces.

Jess (oncall): Closing page for immediate mitigation (flag off). We'll schedule a deep-dive with eng-runtime + SRE + CS in triage channel.

Marta (cs): I'll notify the three affected customers with a brief: "We observed transient higher-latency from a canary rollout; rollback applied and performance restored; follow-up and postmortem forthcoming."

Sam (eng-runtime): Action items: 1) reproduce locally with prefetch_v2 on specific token patterns, 2) add defensive limits in batcher, 3) include canary memory headroom checks in rollout policy.

Nayna (sre): I'm creating incident doc and will assign owners. Handoff to Raj in 10m.

Jess (oncall): Thanks all. If anything regresses, re-open. :thumbsup:
